name: Data Room Diligence
title: Data Room Diligence
answer: Data room diligence is the review of a target company's documents before a deal closes, and in AI-related transactions it now covers model weights, training data, evaluation results and vendor contracts alongside the usual financial and legal files. The work sits with deal teams, technical advisers and outside counsel, who must read an asset that changes faster than a normal set of accounts. Because AI companies often hold few physical assets, the data room is frequently the main place where value and liability can actually be seen.

crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

sections.body: Data room diligence is the review of a target company's documents before a deal closes, and in AI-related transactions it now covers model weights, training data, evaluation results and vendor contracts alongside the usual financial and legal files. The work sits with deal teams, technical advisers and outside counsel, who must read an asset that changes faster than a normal set of accounts. Because AI companies often hold few physical assets, the data room is frequently the main place where value and liability can actually be seen.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: The room itself is usually a virtual data room hosted by a vendor, with permissions, watermarks and an audit trail of who opened which file. Inside it, AI targets add artefacts that older rooms did not carry: dataset licences, model cards, benchmark runs, inference cost sheets and cloud commitments. Buyers increasingly ask for a reproducible environment or a sandbox where a model can be queried, because a static PDF of results proves little on its own.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: Teams work through an index of requests, then split review by workstream, with counsel on contracts and IP, finance on revenue and cost, and technical advisers on data provenance and model performance. Findings are logged in a tracker, scored by severity, and turned into questions, then into representations, warranties and indemnities in the purchase agreement. On AI deals the technical review often runs in parallel with the legal one, since a licence problem in a training set is also a contract problem.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: The core risks are provenance of training data, rights to use model outputs, open source licence obligations, privacy of personal data in the corpus, and exposure to regulation or litigation. Diligence has to establish where each dataset came from, what consent or licence covers it, and whether the target can keep using the model after closing.Nothing in a data room review is legal advice, and findings should be tested by qualified counsel in the relevant jurisdiction.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: Expect data rooms to become more standardised, with model cards, dataset lineage records and evaluation reports treated as ordinary disclosure items rather than extras. Buyers are likely to ask for post-closing access to retrain or audit a model, and for escrow of weights and data where the seller's team is small. As regulation settles, the diligence checklist will converge on a common set of questions, though the underlying technology will keep outrunning the paperwork.
